titulo: Roy Sullivan: Struck by Lightning 7 Times #shorts
premisa: Título: 'Roy Sullivan: Struck by Lightning 7 Times' (41 car.). Cuenta por golpes en segunda persona, unas 150 palabras, 52-58 s. Guion: 'Strike number one: you're up a fire tower. The bolt rips through your leg and blows off your big toenail. [1942] Twenty-seven years pass. You're driving a mountain road. Strike two. Your eyebrows? Gone. You black out at the wheel. [1969] Next summer, your own front yard. Strike three. Your left shoulder is seared. [1970] Strike four: inside the ranger station. Your hair catches fire. [1972] At Shenandoah National Park, coworkers start keeping their distance in storms. They call you the Human Lightning Rod. Your name is Roy Sullivan. Strike five: you see a storm cloud and drive away. It follows you. You step out of the truck. Bam. Hair on fire. Again. [1973] Strike six: on patrol. A cloud tracks you. You run. It wins. [1976] Strike seven: you're fishing. Burns on your chest and stomach. [1977] Then a bear walks up and tries to steal your trout. You hit it with a tree branch. Seven strikes. One man. Guinness World Records: the most lightning strikes ever survived. Official holder: Roy Sullivan.' Corte seco.
